---
title: "Self-hosting"
subtitle: "Running the server yourself, which is the only way it runs"
---

::: {.callout-important}
**Partly implemented.** The server, its configuration, the three storage backends, tokens, backup
and restore all exist and are tested. The Docker image and compose file in `deploy/` are written and
have **never been run**; the metrics endpoint, the sidecar profiles and the enrichment keys belong to
later phases. Each section below says which it is.
:::

Recueil has no hosted edition and no account. You run it, or it does not run. That constrains the
design usefully: the default deployment has to be a single process with a single file behind it,
and everything heavier has to be optional.

## Requirements

| | Minimum | Comfortable |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | 2 cores | 4 cores; OCR and GROBID are the hungry parts |
| RAM | 1 GB | 4 GB, or 8 GB with the GROBID sidecar |
| Disk | Your library, plus about 15% | Same, on something you back up |
| Runtime | Docker, or Node 22 LTS | Docker, for the sidecar profiles |
| Database | None. SQLite is the default and v1 is SQLite only ([ADR-0015](adr.qmd)) | |

Recueil runs on `amd64` and `arm64`, so a Raspberry Pi or an ARM NAS is a reasonable host for a
single-user library — with the caveat that OCR and GROBID will be slow enough that you will want to
run them elsewhere or not at all.

## Deployment shapes

### Docker (the reference deployment)

The `deploy/` directory holds a `docker-compose.yml` with the server, and the heavy optional
components behind **compose profiles** so that none of them start unless you ask.

None of the compose profiles has been run. They are written from the upstream images' documented
interfaces and are a starting point, not a tested deployment.

| Profile | Service | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| *(none)* | `recueil` | The server. SQLite, local file storage, FTS5 search. |
| `ocr` | OCRmyPDF / Tesseract worker | A text layer on scans |
| `grobid` | GROBID | Scholarly PDF metadata, reference lists, in-text citation contexts |
| `search` | Meilisearch | Search for libraries that have outgrown FTS5 ([ADR-0011](adr.qmd)) |
| `translation` | `zotero/translation-server` | Import by URL, DOI, PMID, ISBN, arXiv |
| `intent` | SciCite | Local classification of citation intent |

```sh
docker compose --profile ocr --profile grobid up -d
```

Start with none of them. Add one when you have a reason you can name.

### Desktop

The Tauri 2 shell bundles the same server binary as a sidecar on `localhost` (Phase 4). Same code,
same database file, no container. It adds watched folders, a tray icon, the `recueil://item/<id>`
URI scheme for deep links out of Overleaf or Quarto, and open-in-external-app.

### From source

```sh
pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm --filter @recueil/server start
```

## Configuration

Configuration is environment variables, because that is what containers, systemd and secret
managers all already speak. Every variable has a default that works.

These are the variables the server reads today. It refuses to start on an invalid one, naming every
offender, rather than falling back to a default.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `RECUEIL_DATABASE_URL` | `file:./data/recueil.db` | A path, a `file:`/`sqlite:` URL, or `:memory:` |
| `RECUEIL_STORAGE_PATH` | `./data/storage` | Root of the content-addressed store. Resolved to an absolute path |
| `RECUEIL_PORT` | `3000` | Listen port. `0` asks the OS for a free one |
| `RECUEIL_HOST` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address. The container image sets `0.0.0.0` |
| `RECUEIL_BASE_URL` | — | Public URL behind a reverse proxy; also the `servers` entry of the served OpenAPI document |
| `RECUEIL_LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | `trace` … `fatal`, or `silent`; output is structured JSON |
| `RECUEIL_CORS_ORIGIN` | — | Comma-separated origins, or `*`. Unset means no cross-origin browser access |
| `RECUEIL_TRUST_PROXY` | `false` | Trust `X-Forwarded-*`. Only behind a proxy you control |
| `RECUEIL_REQUIRE_AUTH` | `false` | Refuse an unauthenticated `/api/v1` call. **Turn it on for anything reachable beyond loopback** |
| `RECUEIL_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` | `536870912` | Ceiling on one uploaded file, enforced during the streaming hash |
| `RECUEIL_SECRET_KEY` | — | 32 bytes, base64 or hex, encrypting stored source and backend credentials. **Unset means the server will not store a credential at all** — there is deliberately no derived fallback |
| `RECUEIL_INGEST_ALLOWED_ROOTS` | — | Comma-separated absolute directories a watched folder may be pointed at. Set it wherever the token holder and the machine owner differ |
| `RECUEIL_INGEST_ALLOW_PRIVATE_TARGETS` | `false` | Let a WebDAV source or storage backend reach a loopback, link-local or private address. See below |
| `RECUEIL_INGEST_SCRATCH_PATH` | OS temp | Where archives are expanded. Needs room for the largest one |
| `RECUEIL_INGEST_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` | `0.75` | The stage-9 gate. Below it a document is stored and queued for review |
| `RECUEIL_OCR_ENGINE` | `none` | `none` or `ocrmypdf`. See the caveat below |
| `RECUEIL_OCR_BINARY` | `ocrmypdf` | The executable, or a wrapper around one |
| `RECUEIL_OCR_LANGUAGES` | — | Tesseract codes, comma-separated, in preference order (`deu,eng`) |
| `RECUEIL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `10000` | How long a shutdown waits for in-flight requests |

The enrichment keys — `RECUEIL_CROSSREF_MAILTO`, `RECUEIL_OPENALEX_KEY`, `RECUEIL_UNPAYWALL_EMAIL`
and the rest — arrive with the resolvers in Phase 3 and are not read yet. `_FILE`-suffixed variants
for Docker and Kubernetes secrets are planned and not implemented.

### Where a source may point

A source URL and a storage-backend URL are addresses the server dials on somebody else's say-so, so
by default it refuses to dial anything internal: loopback, link-local (including `169.254.169.254`,
the cloud metadata address), the RFC 1918 ranges, unique-local and multicast. The check runs on the
address the connection actually carries, not on the one the form was given, because a name may
resolve publicly while the source is being created and to `127.0.0.1` by the time anything connects
to it.

`RECUEIL_INGEST_ALLOW_PRIVATE_TARGETS=true` turns the rule off wholesale, which is what a NAS in the
cupboard needs. It is off by default because it is the operator saying "the inside of my network is
a place this server may reach", and that is a sentence somebody should have to write down.

Two consequences worth knowing: a WebDAV URL carrying a password in its userinfo
(`https://user:pass@host/dav/`) has the credential taken out on ingress and moved into the
`RECUEIL_SECRET_KEY` store, so it is never written to `ingestion_sources.config` and never comes
back from the API; and a failed connection check reports the status and the reason but not the
target's response body.

### OCR

`RECUEIL_OCR_ENGINE=ocrmypdf` turns stage 5 on against an `ocrmypdf` binary on `PATH`; point
`RECUEIL_OCR_BINARY` at a wrapper script if you would rather run it in a container. The default is
`none` because nothing may be assumed installed, and one missing binary would otherwise put an
identical failure on every scan.

**The adapter has not been run against a real OCRmyPDF in this repository.** The test suite exercises
the `OcrEngine` interface through an in-process fake — a suite that needs a container is a suite
nobody runs — so treat the integration as unproven until you have watched one scan through it.

A further limit worth knowing: the decision to OCR is taken per *document*, not per page. A PDF whose
first page carries a text layer and whose second is a scan is treated as having a text layer, and the
scanned page is neither recognised nor indexed.

## Storage backends

The content store is pluggable, and the choice is per-instance rather than per-item.

| Backend | Notes | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Local filesystem | Content-addressed layout derived from the SHA-256. The default | Implemented |
| WebDAV | A Nextcloud or ownCloud share as the store | Implemented; tested against a local WebDAV server, not against Nextcloud |
| S3 | Any S3-compatible object store; MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi | Implemented; tested against a local in-process S3 fake, not against AWS or MinIO |

All three pass one shared conformance suite of sixteen cases — hashing, streaming, the empty blob,
the multipart path, concurrent puts of the same bytes, repair of a truncated blob, detection of rot
that kept the length — so they are interchangeable rather than merely similarly named. One
difference is declared rather than smoothed over: the two remote backends verify the digest as they
read and fail the read on a mismatch; the local one hands back what is on disk and offers `verify()`
separately.

Whichever you choose, the layout is documented and derived from the hash, so the store can be read,
verified and re-imported without the application running. That is the concrete meaning of the
no-lock-in principle.

## Reverse proxy and TLS

Recueil speaks plain HTTP and expects a reverse proxy — Caddy, nginx, Traefik — to terminate TLS. It
does not manage certificates, because your proxy already does it better.

```caddy
recueil.example.org {
    reverse_proxy localhost:8080
}
```

Set `RECUEIL_BASE_URL` to the public URL. The server needs it for connector callbacks, webhook
payloads, `.bib` endpoint URLs and the SSE stream.

**Do not put it on the open internet unless you mean to.** A Tailscale or WireGuard network is the
right answer for a personal library, and the deployment is designed for it.

## Authentication

Single user in v1, with scoped API tokens; the schema is shaped for users and groups so that
multi-user can be added later without a painful migration.

- **Session auth** for the web UI.
- **Scoped bearer tokens** for everything else — the CLI, scripts, the R and Python packages, the
  MCP server, a `.bib` URL you paste into Overleaf.
- Every token is named, scoped, revocable and shown with its last-used timestamp.
- Every write is attributed in the audit log to the token that made it, including writes made by an
  LLM through MCP. There is no anonymous mutation.

A `.bib` endpoint token is the one credential you will be tempted to paste somewhere careless. Scope
it to read-only on one collection.

## Backup and restore

```sh
recueil backup --to /backups/recueil
recueil restore --from /backups/recueil/2026-08-22
```

A backup is a consistent snapshot of the database, a manifest of the file store and the
configuration, in a layout designed for `restic` to deduplicate well. Because the store is content
addressed and append-only in practice, incremental backups are cheap.

**Restore is exercised in CI.** A backup procedure that has never been restored is a hypothesis.

## Monitoring

- `GET /health` — liveness and readiness, with the database and each configured sidecar reported
  separately.
- `GET /metrics` — Prometheus format: queue depth, job durations and failures, resolver call counts
  and rate-limit state per source, ingestion throughput, review-queue size.
- Structured JSON logs on stdout, with a correlation id per request and per job.

The two numbers worth alerting on for a personal instance are **review-queue size** and **failed
jobs**. Both mean something is waiting for you.

## Upgrades

Migrations run automatically at start and are forward-only. Take a backup first; the release notes
will say so too. Multi-arch images are published to `ghcr.io`, and version pinning is supported and
recommended. Until 1.0, the data model may change under a migration and the plugin API may break
between minor versions — see [ADR-0014](adr.qmd) for what is and is not promised before then.
